title: Uddhava Dasa of Gadadhara's Branch
html:
A Branch of Gadadhara Pandita

Sri Uddhava Dasa is one of the branches (shakha) of the tree of Gadadhara Pandita Gosvami, the eternal associate of Sri Chaitanya. Kavi Karnapura calls him “Shriman Uddhava Dasa,” and Yadunandana Dasa, a disciple of Gadadhara, “Shrimad Uddhava Dasa.” Krishnadasa Kaviraja Gosvami, listing the branches of Gadadhara in the “Chaitanya-charitamrita,” places him in a single line with three other devotees:

“Srinatha Chakravarti, Uddhava Dasa, Jitamitra and Jagannatha Dasa of Kashthakata.” (CC, Adi 12.83)1

Beyond this the primary sources say almost nothing of his life. Neither his birthplace nor his family is known, nor the year and day of his appearance, nor when and where he left this world; his days are not in the Vaishnava calendar of the Sri Chaitanya Saraswat Math either. All that has come down to us about him is a few lines: a place in the list of branches, the praise of a disciple of Gadadhara, and Karnapura's word about his eternal nature.

Giver of Prema to the Lowly

Yadunandana Dasa, a disciple of Gadadhara Pandita, devotes a separate verse in the “Shakha-nirnayamrita” (“The Nectar of Determining the Branches”) to each of his guru's disciples. Of Uddhava Dasa he says:

“I worship Shrimad Uddhava Dasa, full of virtues, who bestows the whole wealth of prema upon the most lowly.” (“Shakha-nirnayamrita,” 35)2

Srila Bhaktisiddhanta Sarasvati Thakura quotes this verse in his “Anubhashya” on the same verse of the “Charitamrita” (Adi 12.83), and one of the biographies refers the reader there for information about him. But the “Anubhashya,” too, has nothing about him beyond this verse.

The verse is brief, yet it says the essential. The wealth of prema, divine love for Krishna, is not won by learning, noble birth or austerity; Uddhava Dasa bestowed it on those who counted themselves lowest of all — the humble and the fallen. In this he followed his guru and Mahaprabhu Himself, Who gave prema to all without distinction.

An Avesha of the Moon

Who he is in the Lord's eternal pastimes Kavi Karnapura tells in the “Gaura-ganoddesha-dipika”:

“The discerning should know Acharya Chandrashekhara as Chandra (the Moon); Sriman Uddhava Dasa too is an empowered incarnation (avesha-avatara) of the Moon.” (GGD 112)

In the same verse Acharya Chandrashekhara is called the Moon itself; Uddhava Dasa is one in whom the Moon is present by its potency (avesha)3. This is Karnapura's word about the eternal nature of an associate, not about a rebirth in the worldly sense: the Lord's servants come into the world together with Him, by His will, and remain who they are in His eternal pastimes.

Welcoming Jahnava

The biographies do not cite it, but Uddhava apparently appears once more in the “Bhakti-ratnakara.” When Jahnava Devi, the eternal consort of Nityananda, was going to the great festival at Kheturi, many mahantas met her at Kantaka-nagara — Katwa. Among them Narahari Chakravarti names Shivananda, Vaninatha, Vallabha, Chaitanya Dasa, Hari Acharya, Bhagavatacharya, Nartaka-Gopala, Jitamishra, Raghu Mishra, Kashinatha Pandita, Nayana Mishra, Jagannatha of Kashthakata, Pushpa-Gopala, Raghunatha, Lakshminatha Pandita — and “generous Uddhava” (“Bhakti-ratnakara,” 10.414–418). Almost all these names also stand in the list of Gadadhara's branch in the “Charitamrita” (Adi 12.79–87); so this Uddhava is most probably Uddhava Dasa of Gadadhara's branch4.

If so, then even after the Lord's disappearance he remained among the disciples of Gadadhara and with them welcomed Jahnava with honour on her way.

Namesakes

Several Vaishnavas bore the name Uddhava Dasa, and the accounts of them are easily confused. The reference work “Gaudiya-vaishnava-abhidhana” names, besides our Uddhava, two more (according to one of the biographies, at least two).

The first lived in Vraja, in a hut by Pavana-sarovara at Nandagrama, performed his bhajana there and was a follower of Sanatana Gosvami5.

The second is the renowned composer of padas Sri Uddhava Dasa of the village of Tenya (Teyagram) in Murshidabad district. By birth he was named Sri Krishnakanta Majumdar; he received mantra from Sri Radhamohana Thakura and, according to one of the biographies, composed many songs about the pastimes of Radha and Krishna.

Uddhava Dasa in Vrindavana

Of the Uddhava Dasa who lived in Vrindavana the primary sources say more, and the biographies give this information in the chapter on our Uddhava: one without reservation, another plainly taking them to be one person. Neither the “Charitamrita” nor the “Bhakti-ratnakara” says so, and the identity (like the difference) cannot be proved6. We therefore tell of the Vrindavana Uddhava separately.

When Sri Rupa Gosvami was living in Vrindavana, in his old age he could no longer make the journey to Govardhana, to the Deity of Gopala, though he longed with all his heart to see Him (Rupa and Sanatana had never dared to climb the hill of Govardhana itself). Seeing this longing, Gopala Himself, as if out of fear of the mlecchas, came to Mathura and lived at the home of Vitthalanatha, Vallabha Bhatta's younger son. So Rupa received His darshana:

“For fear of the mlecchas Gopala came to the city of Mathura and stayed for a month in the house of Vitthaleshvara. Then Rupa Gosani took all his associates with him, stayed in Mathura for a month and had darshana of Gopala.” (CC, Madhya 18.47–48)

Among those with whom Rupa beheld Gopala, Krishnadasa Kaviraja also names Uddhava Dasa:

“Sri Uddhava Dasa and Madhava, Sri Gopala Dasa and Narayana Dasa…” (CC, Madhya 18.51)7

Later, when Srinivasa Acharya came to Vrindavana, he visited the hut of Sanatana Gosvami in Nandishvara, where Vaishnavas welcomed him, and the “Bhakti-ratnakara” says: “Sri Uddhava Dasa, Madhava and all who were there met one another and were overjoyed” (5.1333)8. Srinivasa and Raghava Gosvami, going round Vrindavana-dhama, came to Uddhava Dasa more than once, and each time he received them and served them with the greatest love.

And when Srinivasa Acharya, together with Narottama Thakura and Shyamananda, set out for Bengal with the books of the Gosvamis on an ox cart, given to them by Sri Jiva, the Vaishnavas of Vrindavana gathered to see them off, and among them was Uddhava Dasa. Narahari Chakravarti names:

“Sri Govinda, the most generous Vani Krishnadasa, and Sri Uddhava, who from time to time went to Gauda.” (“Bhakti-ratnakara,” 6.514)9

These words — “from time to time went to Gauda” — are the only thread that could link the Vrindavana Uddhava with the Bengal branch of Gadadhara. But no identity can be asserted on it.

Significance

Little is known of Uddhava Dasa of Gadadhara's branch, but that little comes from the most trustworthy witnesses. The “Charitamrita” counts him among the branches of Gadadhara Pandita; a disciple of Gadadhara praises him as one who bestows the whole wealth of prema on the most lowly; Kavi Karnapura reveals that the Moon is present in him. His life is one of those quiet branches of the great tree of devotion which, leaving no loud stories behind, bore the fruit of prema for the fallen.

Notes

  1. In the older edition of the translation of the “Charitamrita” this verse is numbered Adi 12.84. One of the biographies quotes the line with the name “Kashinatha Chakravarti”; the Gaudiya Math edition and the “Anubhashya” read “Srinatha Chakravarti,” and the “Anubhashya” gives for him the verse of the “Shakha-nirnayamrita” (13) about “the pandita named Srinatha.”
  2. One of the biographies quotes the verse with the reading “-chitta” (“bestows a heart full of prema”); another and the “Anubhashya” read “-vitta” (“the whole wealth of prema”), as in our translation. The biographies call the author of the “Shakha-nirnayamrita” Yadunatha Dasa, the “Anubhashya” Yadunandana Dasa; we follow the “Anubhashya.”
  3. The verse does not say which Uddhava Dasa is meant; one of the biographies refers it to Gadadhara's branch, while the “Anubhashya” on Adi 12.83 does not quote it. That biography also numbers the verse “192,” whereas in its chapter on Chandrashekhara the same verse is 112, as in our edition of the “Gaura-ganoddesha-dipika.”
  4. The biographies do not cite this passage; referring “generous Uddhava” to Gadadhara's branch rests on the make-up of the list and remains probable, not proven. In an edition of the “Bhakti-ratnakara” with different numbering it is 10.404–408.
  5. According to one of the biographies, simply “in Vraja, on the bank of Pavana-sarovara,” without Nandagrama.
  6. These are Vrindavana Vaishnavas of Rupa Gosvami's last years and of Srinivasa Acharya's time; no primary source places them in Gadadhara's branch.
  7. According to one of the biographies, Uddhava Dasa stayed with Rupa at Gopala's side “for more than a month”; by the “Charitamrita” (Madhya 18.47–48, 54), for a month. One of the biographies attaches to this episode a reference to “Bhakti-ratnakara” 5.1333; in fact that verse describes the meeting with Srinivasa.
  8. The biographies say that Srinivasa and Raghava came to the hut of Uddhava Dasa himself. By the “Bhakti-ratnakara” (5.1330–1334), Srinivasa came to the hut of Sanatana in Nandishvara, where Gopala Mishra, the son of Sanatana's priest and Sanatana's disciple, was staying, and there he met Uddhava Dasa, Madhava and others; there was a great festival, and the night was spent in nama-sankirtana. This agrees with the reference work, by which the Vrindavana Uddhava lived at Pavana-sarovara near Nandagrama.
  9. By the “Bhakti-ratnakara” (6.509–542), the Vaishnavas, Uddhava among them, gathered at the temple of Govinda in Vrindavana; the cart set off on the road to Mathura, and the Gosvamis walked beside it for some time, and from Mathura onward Jiva escorted it. One of the biographies writes that Uddhava went part of the way with them “from Mathura towards North Bengal”; in the “Bhakti-ratnakara” it is from Vrindavana, and the goal of the journey is Gauda.
